description: How both packages expand governed-definition tokens and render definitions into the prompt. The source is tests/shared/definition-rendering.json; the copy under pkg-r/tests/testthat/fixtures/shared/ is generated by scripts/sync-shared-fixtures.sh. Edit the source and re-run that script. The R suite runs these cases against the implementation; the Python suite checks the fixture's integrity until its registry lands, then runs them too.

records.description: Export records keyed by a fixture-local id, in the shape both packages hydrate: pkg-py builds ExportRecord, pkg-r builds a row of the registry data frame. A null scalar is a field data-dict omitted.

survey_mixed_temporal.name: mixed temporal case
survey_mixed_temporal.expression: CASE WHEN done THEN taken_on ELSE taken_at END

expand_tokens.description: expand_tokens(sql, records): which queries expand, and to what. `expanded` is the resulting SQL, or null when the query must be refused. `applied` names the records reported alongside the result. A refused case carries a `reason` slug; each package maps the slug to its own message, since the wording is idiomatic to the language and only the refusal is shared.
expand_tokens.rule: Every token resolves against the query as written. A bare token binds to the definition whose table appears in the query, and compiled SQL introduced by an earlier expansion does not make a table appear.

cases.name: a bare token expands against its own table
several tokens on one table all expand
a bare token whose table is absent is refused
an earlier expansion does not bring its tables into scope
a token no definition matches is refused
a bare token defined on two tables in the query is refused
cases.sql: SELECT {{other}} FROM sales JOIN returns ON returns.id = sales.id

cases.name: qualifying resolves what the bare token could not
cases.sql: SELECT {{returns::other}} FROM sales JOIN returns ON returns.id = sales.id
cases.expanded: SELECT (count(*)) FROM sales JOIN returns ON returns.id = sales.id

gist.description: The one-line summary rendered for a definition, used in the first-touch entry and in every retrieval chunk. Shows the compiled SQL, never the authored expression.
gist.rule: `(kind, type)` when data-dict inferred a type, `(kind)` alone when it did not. The rest of the gist is unaffected by an absent type.

cases.name: kind and type, with a description
cases.expected: (metric, number) Revenue over all order lines. Selected SQL(duckdb): `(sum(revenue))`.

cases.name: description, details and translation notes all appear
cases.expected: (filter, boolean) EMEA rows only. Matches the dictionary enum exactly. Selected SQL(duckdb): `("region" = 'EMEA')`. Translation notes: Case-sensitive comparison.

cases.name: an absent type is left out and the rest of the gist survives
cases.expected: (derived) When the response was captured. Selected SQL(duckdb): `(CASE WHEN "done" THEN "taken_on" ELSE "taken_at" END)`.

index.description: The kind index shown in the system prompt, one line per table, truncated to a character cap. `overflows` is what tells the model to search instead of trusting the index.
index.rule: The cap applies to the rendered text, so the newlines joining the lines count against it.

cases.name: every line fits under the default cap
cases.text:
- sales: filters `{{emea}}`; metrics `{{total}}`
- returns: metrics `{{other}}`
- survey: derived `{{mixed temporal case}}`

cases.name: the joining newline counts against the cap
one more character admits the second line
